info.title: Ship Daemon API
info.description: HTTP surface for the Ship daemon (shipd). Covers auth pairing, workspace + job + spec management, artifacts, collections, views, mesh + actor routing, hook ingress, and the public webhook trigger. Bearer auth is required by default; public operations carry an empty `security` override.

post.description:
Injected state:
- `Extension<SharedWebhookSource>` — the webhook registry from HookEngine
- `Extension<SharedKernelRef>` — shared kernel for event emission

Authentication is hook-declared: each trigger in `.ship/hooks/` carries
its own `secret`, which must be supplied via the `x-ship-webhook-secret`
request header. Callers that send the wrong secret (or none at all for
a trigger that requires one) get `401`. Bearer auth is explicitly not
used — see `security = []` in the OpenAPI decoration.

Rate limiting is per-trigger as configured at hook definition time;
exceeding the limit yields `429`.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Trigger path as declared under .ship/hooks/. Matches the `*path` glob from the router.

requestBody.description: Raw request body forwarded to the trigger's handler. Content-type is opaque to the daemon.

404.description: No trigger registered for this path

get.description:
Returns each `JobRecord` with two operator-visibility annotations:

- `process_state`: `"alive"` when the latest process projection for the
  slug is still Running, `"missing"` when the most recent supervisor
  sweep flagged drift (no_process) without a coherence_restored after
  it, `"terminal"` for jobs in a terminal status, `"none"` otherwise.
- `notes`: optional truncated error / blocker for the row's NOTES column.

post.summary: POST /api/runtime/jobs — emit job.created event through the kernel.
post.description:
The kernel persists the event and routes it to subscribers.
The job_dispatch service handles all heavy lifting (worktree creation,
dependency resolution, agent spawning).

post.summary: POST /api/runtime/jobs/end — signal that a provider turn ended for a job.
post.description:
Called by the session Stop hook when an agent finishes a response turn.
For multi-step pipeline jobs, this sends a TurnEnded signal to the step
monitor (which accumulates evidence before deciding to advance).
For single-step jobs, emits job.completed directly.

post.summary:
POST /api/runtime/jobs/{slug}/cancel — emit `job.cancelled` for the
job with this slug. Idempotent: returns 409 with the current status
when the job is already in a terminal state, and emits no event.

get.description:

`/api/runtime` so subsequent fetches from the served document
authenticate without needing the query token. The auth middleware
has already validated the caller's token/session before we run.

get.description:
Returns only active workspaces. Archived/dead workspaces are excluded
from the API surface — the reconciler handles cleanup internally.

Upgrades to WebSocket or returns 404/429 before the upgrade.
WebSocketUpgrade is extracted manually after validation so tests can reach
the 404/429 paths without a live HTTP connection (which axum requires for
upgrade state — without it the extractor returns 426 before the handler runs).

post.summary: POST /api/session/register — issue a scoped session token for an MCP agent.
post.description:
Requires daemon token authentication. The MCP server calls this during
startup. The daemon computes scopes from the agent's role and returns a
session token the MCP server uses for all subsequent requests.

Role escalation is prevented: only callers with `Scope::Full` (daemon
token holders) can issue sessions, and the "contributor" role (which
grants Full) is blocked — agents must use "worker", "lead", or
"commander".

200.description: Session token minted for the agent role

headless.description:
When true, force the headless (ProcessExecutor) path. When false or
absent, the default TmuxWindowExecutor (tmux-window) path is used.

source_spec_path.description:
Operator-facing path to the spec file (absolute when resolvable).
Plumbed into the JobRecord so `ship jobs` can distinguish which
spec each job was dispatched from. Distinct from `spec_path`
(daemon-side worktree destination). Optional: `--spec-text`
dispatches and legacy callers send `None`.

spec_content.description:
Inline spec content. Travels in the JobCreated event; the worktree
adapter writes it to `spec_path` at dispatch time.

vars.description:
Pipeline variables for `{{ var }}` interpolation in step fields.
Merged over pipeline-file defaults; CLI `--var` flags land here.

ErrorResponse.description:
Canonical error body returned by non-2xx responses.

Handlers today emit `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` or
`{"ok": false, "data": "..."}`. The spec standardizes on this richer
shape so SDK consumers can branch on a machine-readable `error` code
without parsing the human-readable message.

details.description:
Optional structured details. Shape varies by endpoint — see the
individual operation for specifics.

message.description: Human-readable error message. Safe to surface in UIs and logs.

GenericOk.description: Generic OK acknowledgement for endpoints whose only signal is success.

HookResponse.description: Hook response: allow or block with reason.

body.description:
Arbitrary JSON broadcast payload. Delivered to every agent whose
capabilities match `capability_filter` (or all agents when unset).

data.description:
Response payload; shape varies by endpoint. See individual operation
responses for concrete shapes. Represented as arbitrary JSON because
this envelope is reused across dozens of handlers that return
heterogeneous bodies (lists, single records, ack strings, error
details, etc.).

ok.description: `true` on success; `false` when the handler returned a structured error.

body.description:
Arbitrary JSON message body. Delivered verbatim to the target agent's
`mesh.send` event; schema is caller-defined.

token_prefix.description:
If set, revoke only sessions whose token starts with this prefix.
If unset AND `all` is true, revoke every non-ephemeral session.

Scope.description:
Coarse-grained capability scopes for daemon session access control.
Each handler declares which scope it requires; the auth layer checks
the session's granted scopes before the handler runs.

token_prefix.description: First 12 chars of the token for display — never the full value.

value.description:
Setting value as JSON. Shape depends on the setting (string, bool,
number, or structured object). Validated against the setting's
registered schema before persist.

ShipHookEvent.description: Normalized hook event sent by Claude HTTP hooks or the `ship hook` adapter.

WebhookAck.description: Minimal acknowledgement returned by webhook ingress.

ok.description: Always `true` when the trigger accepted the request.

bearer_token.description: Daemon bearer token — found in ~/.ship/daemon.token after `ship daemon start`. Also accepted: session tokens minted by /auth/pair/confirm or /auth/server-attest.
